Discussion)**\\n> - exp-015 完整 3 模型结果（frozen self-embeddings + MLP probe, each model probing its own generations）:\\n>   - Qwen-cont: K*(neural)=3, 2v3 AUC=0.6159, CI [0.6099, 0.6223], CI lower > 0.60 ✅\\n>   - Pythia-1.4B: K*(neural)=2, 2v3 AUC=0.5963, CI [0.5892, 0.6033], CI lower < 0.60 ❌\\n>   - OLMo-1B: K*(neural)=2, 2v3 AUC=0.5892, CI [0.5818, 0.5965], CI lower < 0.60 ❌\\n> - **K*(neural) 不具备 universality**：仅 Qwen-cont 达到 K*=3，Pythia/OLMo 仍为 K*=2\\n> - **Self-familiarity 解释**：每个模型用自己的 frozen embeddings 探测自己生成的文本。Qwen 对 Qwen-generated 文本更敏感（self-familiarity），K*=3 是 model-specific artifact 而非 universal signal\\n> - **K*(theory) ≥ 3 弱化**：只能 claim \\\"K*(theory) ≥ 3 for Qwen representations\\\"，不能泛化为所有模型\\n> - **Interpretability–deployability tradeoff 加强**：15D features 给出 universal K*=2（3/3 模型一致），neural probe 给出 model-dependent K*∈{2,3}。Model-free 方案的 universality 优势在 cross-model 结果下更明显\\n> - 所有 3 模型 neural 2v3 AUC > lgbm 2v3 AUC（+3.9pp 到 +5.5pp），说明 learned representations 确实恢复了额外 depth signal，但不足以在所有模型上推过 θ=0.60\\n> - 论文定位：**正面发现**——cross-model validation 揭示 K*(neural) 是 representation-dependent，验证了选择 model-free 15D features 作为 headline K* characterization 的正确性\\n> - 预防审稿人 \\\"why bury the stronger result?\\\"：K*(neural)=3 仅对 Qwen 成立且是 self-familiarity driven，不适合作为 headline result；15D K*=2 的 universality（10/10 conditions + 3/3 models）才是可靠可部署的结论\\n\\n**(d) 61-63%\\n> - Feature subset: cont→rw 89% > rw→cont 82% → continuation features 是 rewrite 的通用子集\\n> - Interpretation: rewrite mode 的 instruction-following 引入 mode-specific style artifacts，放大 depth signal 但降低跨模型泛化性\\n> - 论文定位：Analysis subsection（\\\"How does generation mode affect depth estimation?\\\"），不是独立 claim\\n\\n### Secondary: C3 (K*-Aware Data Curation Validation)\\nK*=2 correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit: binary K*-aware filtering (0.5941 MMLU) outperforms graduated depth weighting (best 0.5892 at α=0.9), surprisal-based selection (0.5894), and DSIR distribution matching (~0.5867, ≈ no-filter level). K* serves as an actionable curation guideline — the discrimination boundary directly determines the optimal filtering granularity.\\n\\n### Supporting Analysis: Canonical Condition Selection\\nGeneration mode 是 depth estimation 的显著混淆变量。Methodology 段落阐述 continuation mode 作为 canonical condition 的选择及理由（不作为独立 claim）。\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: Web 数据正被多代递归合成文本污染。当前检测方法将合成文本视为 binary 类别（real vs synthetic），但质量随代际深度非线性退化——首代合成文本与四代合成文本的质量差异巨大却被忽视。\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (DivEye, Min-K%++) 不区分代际；model collapse 文献 (Shumailov et al., Alemohammad et al. 2024, Dohmatob et al. 2024) 描述宏观现象但不提供检测工具；data selection methods (DSIR, D4, DoReMi) 做分布匹配但不估计递归深度；Drayson et al. (2025) 将 binary MGT detection 应用于 importance resampling 以防止 model collapse，是目前最接近的工作。然而这些方法均做二值判断，**不估计文本经历了多少轮递归生成，也不量化辨别能力的饱和边界。**\\n- **Our framing**: 将递归生成建模为 iterated lossy channel，从信息论（DPI）推导出 K* 的必然存在。K* 是首次系统测量的 operational quantity——它告诉数据策展者\\\"在什么深度以下，depth-aware curation 比 binary detection 更有价值\\\"。通过 10 条件实验矩阵（5 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies + 1 cross-scale 7B）系统表征 K*，揭示其 universality：**K*=2 在所有 10 个测试条件下不变**，表明递归生成存在一个与具体模型架构和解码策略无关的 universal discrimination boundary。这一发现为数据治理提供 actionable guidance——depth-aware filtering 在 K* 以内有效，且无需针对不同模型或解码配置分别调优。\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"Recursive generation has a universal discrimination boundary at K*=2: invariant across 4 model-mode configurations, 4 decoding strategies, and 1 cross-scale probe (10 conditions total, 1B–7B scale, base+instruct), with cross-model transfer retention of 80-92% confirming depth features are largely text-intrinsic. K*=2 correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit — binary filtering at K* (0.5941 MMLU) outperforms all tested alternatives including graduated weighting, surprisal selection, and DSIR.\\\"\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Responses\\n\\n1. **\\\"Universality claim 只基于小模型，能推广到更大模型吗？\\\"** → exp-004 已将规模扩展至 7B（Qwen2.5-7B, continuation mode, scorer=Qwen2.5-1.5B），K*=2 依然成立，bootstrap 95% CI 确认。结合 4 个 ≤1.5B 架构族（GPT-2 style, Pythia, OLMo, Qwen），K*=2 在 1B–7B 范围内稳定。DPI 理论保证 K*_theory 对任意规模模型存在；进一步扩展至 13B+/70B+ 是重要 future work\\n2. **\\\"只是 feature engineering + off-the-shelf classifier，方法贡献弱\\\"** → 贡献在 problem formulation + empirical characterization（首次测量 K*）+ 理论框架（DPI）+ universality 发现，不是分类器本身\\n3. **\\\"Prompt-chain 不代表真实世界递归污染\\\"** → retrain-chain ecological validity check 作为补充；prompt-chain 是 controlled experiment 的标准方法\\n4. **\\\"K*=2 太浅，graduated filtering 收益有限\\\"** → K*=2 恰好预测了这一结果：binary filtering at K* boundary (0.5941 MMLU) outperforms graduated weighting (best 0.5892), surprisal selection (0.5894), and DSIR (~0.5867). 这验证了 K* 作为 actionable curation guideline 的价值——discrimination boundary 直接决定了最优 filtering 粒度。K* 的 universality 意味着实践者无需为每个模型/解码配置单独标定阈值\\n5. **\\\"同模型做生成和 surprisal 计算有 bias\\\"** → **exp-013 直接反驳**：Pythia↔OLMo 90-92% accuracy retention，0v1 transfer AUC > 0.96。Depth signal 主要编码在文本而非 model self-familiarity\\n6. **\\\"为什么不用 learned representations\\\"** → **exp-015 直接回应**：frozen LLM embeddings + MLP probe 达到 K*=3（vs 15D K*=2），揭示 representation-dependent hierarchy: K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D。Hand-crafted 15D features 的优势在于 model-free transferability（80-92% cross-model retention）、可解释性（支持 degradation ordering 分析）、实用可部署性。Neural representations 多辨别 1 个深度级别但代价是 model dependence + ~100x 计算开销。这一 tradeoff 证明 15D features 是 practical choice，同时表明 theoretical boundary 延伸至 K*=2 之上\\n7. **\\\"Graduated filtering 没和 data selection methods 比\\\"** → exp-006 包含 DSIR baseline + α sensitivity sweep\\n8. **\\\"Decoding strategy 只测了 4 种，coverage 不够\\\"** → 覆盖了实践中最常见的 decoding 配置（greedy, nucleus sampling, temperature scaling high/low）；4/4 完全一致强化 universality claim；extreme decoding（top-k=1 之外的 pathological 配置）留作 future work\\n9. **\\\"为什么不直接用 LLM 做 depth estimation\\\"** → **exp-011 直接反驳**：GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.6 在 500 样本 zero-shot 5-class depth 分类上仅 33.1-33.2% accuracy（MAE ~1.1），低于 OBD 15-feature LightGBM 的 38.6%。二者 binary detection 均 ~88%，说明 LLM 能区分 human vs synthetic 但无法估计递归深度。depth estimation 是非平凡任务，需要专用特征工程\\n\\n## Venue Fit\\n\\n- EMNLP 2026 special theme 明确呼吁 data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance 方向的工作\\n- 2+1 claim 结构：C1' 是 comprehensive characterization study with universality finding，C3 是 practical application，generation mode analysis 增加深度\\n- Universality narrative 比 controllability 更有 impact：从 \\\"K* depends on X, Y, Z\\\" 升级为 \\\"K*=2 is a universal boundary\\\"，审稿人更容易记住和传播\\n- 风险：universality claim 在 ≤1.5B 规模下的外推性是最大攻击面 → 论文中 scope 明确、limitation 诚实、DPI 理论支撑泛化的合理性\\n\", \"total_chars\": 11421, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue

## Canonical Experimental Condition

**Continuation mode 是 cross-model 结论的基础。**

> "We evaluate both generation modes because real-world recursive contamination can arise from either. Our analysis reveals generation mode as a significant confound, leading us to recommend continuation mode as the canonical condition for cross-model comparisons."

| Condition | Pythia↔OLMo | Qwen↔others | 论文定位 |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Continuation | 90-92% retention | 80-85% retention | **主实验条件** — cross-model claims 的基础 |
| Rewrite (instruction) | N/A | 61-63% retention | **upper bound with mode-specific confound** — 仅作 ablation |

**原则**：
- C1' 的跨模型 claim 必须基于 continuation mode 数据

## Core Claims (2+1 结构, D012)

首次系统测量递归合成文本的 generational discrimination boundary K*，并揭示其 universality。

**子组件：**

**(a) K*=2 universality across architectures, generation modes, and decoding strategies**

>
> *Model × mode (exp-007):*
> | Model | AUC 1v2 | 95% CI | CI lower > 0.60? |

> |----------|---------|-----|
> | greedy | 0.6893 | 2 |

> | temp=0.7 | 0.6887 | 2 |
> | temp=1.2 | 0.7039 | 2 |

> - 全部 1v2 CI lower > 0.60, 全部 2v3 CI upper < 0.60, 全部 permutation p < 0.002
> - 4 decoding strategies 的 AUC 1v2 range [0.6866, 0.7039]，K* 完全不变

**(b) Cross-model transfer**

6. **"为什么不用 learned representations"** → **exp-015 直接回应**：frozen LLM embeddings + MLP probe 达到 K*=3（vs 15D K*=2），揭示 representation-dependent hierarchy: K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D。Hand-crafted 15D features 的优势在于 model-free transferability（80-92% cross-model retention）、可解释性（支持 degradation ordering 分析）、实用可部署性。Neural representations 多辨别 1 个深度级别但代价是 model dependence + ~100x 计算开销。这一 tradeoff 证明 15D features 是 practical choice，同时表明 theoretical boundary 延伸至 K*=2 之上
7. **"Graduated filtering 没和 data selection methods 比"** → exp-006 包含 DSIR baseline + α sensitivity sweep
8. **"Decoding strategy 只测了 4 种，coverage 不够"** → 覆盖了实践中最常见的 decoding 配置（greedy, nucleus sampling, temperature scaling high/low）；4/4 完全一致强化 universality claim；extreme decoding（top-k=1 之外的 pathological 配置）留作 future work
9. **"为什么不直接用 LLM 做 depth estimation"** → **exp-011 直接反驳**：GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.6 在 500 样本 zero-shot 5-class depth 分类上仅 33.1-33.2% accuracy（MAE ~1.1），低于 OBD 15-feature LightGBM 的 38.6%。二者 binary detection 均 ~88%，说明 LLM 能区分 human vs synthetic 但无法估计递归深度。depth estimation 是非平凡任务，需要专用特征工程

## Venue Fit

- EMNLP 2026 special theme 明确呼吁 data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance 方向的工作
- 2+1 claim 结构：C1' 是 comprehensive characterization study with universality finding，C3 是 practical application，generation mode analysis 增加深度
- Universality narrative 比 controllability 更有 impact：从 "K* depends on X, Y, Z" 升级为 "K*=2 is a universal boundary"，审稿人更容易记住和传播
- 风险：universality claim 在 ≤1.5B 规模下的外推性是最大攻击面 → 论文中 scope 明确、limitation 诚实、DPI 理论支撑泛化的合理性

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	We evaluate generational depth estimation on six model configurations:
5	Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B in continuation mode, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in both rewrite and continuation modes, Qwen2.5-1.5B (base) in continuation mode, and Qwen2.5-7B in continuation mode (cross-scale scoring with Qwen2.5-1.5B).
6	All experiments use the OBD-LightGBM classifier with the 15-dimensional feature set (Section~\ref{sec:method}), with 5{,}000 texts per depth level (generations 0--5).
7	
8	%% ====================================================================
9	\subsection{$\Kempirical = 2$ Across All Configurations}
10	\label{sec:kstar_boundary}
11	
12	\begin{table*}[t]
13	\centering
14	\small
15	\caption{Pairwise $\auc$ for adjacent depth pairs with bootstrap 95\% CIs and permutation $p$-values for boundary rows.
16	$\Kempirical = 2$ requires 1v2 $\auc > \theta{=}0.60$ and 2v3 $\auc < \theta$; CIs quantify boundary uncertainty.}
17	\label{tab:kstar_ci}
18	\begin{tabular}{lcccccccccc}
19	\toprule
20	 & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Qwen-rw} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Pythia} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{OLMo} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Qwen-cont} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Qwen-7B\rlap{$^\ddagger$}} \\
21	\cmidrule(lr){2-3}\cmidrule(lr){4-5}\cmidrule(lr){6-7}\cmidrule(lr){8-9}\cmidrule(lr){10-11}
22	 & $\auc$ & 95\% CI & $\auc$ & 95\% CI & $\auc$ & 95\% CI & $\auc$ & 95\% CI & $\auc$ & 95\% CI \\
23	\midrule
24	0v1 & .9956 & & .9932 & & .9970 & & .9971 & & .9638 & [.961,\,.967] \\
25	1v2 & .6955 & [.686,\,.704]\rlap{$^*$} & .6539 & [.645,\,.663]\rlap{$^*$} & .6145 & [.605,\,.625]\rlap{$^*$} & .6112 & [.602,\,.621]\rlap{$^*$} & .6168 & [.608,\,.626]\rlap{$^*$} \\
26	2v3 & .5893 & [.580,\,.599] & .5514 & [.542,\,.563] & .5496 & [.540,\,.560] & .5609 & [.551,\,.571] & .5492 & [.539,\,.559] \\
27	3v4 & .5435 & & .5152 & & .5091 & & .5409 & & .5276 & \\
28	4v5 & .5340 & & .5136 & & .5045 & & .5141 & & .5085 & \\
29	\bottomrule
30	\multicolumn{11}{l}{\footnotesize $^*$Permutation $p < 0.001$ for all five 1v2 comparisons.} \\
31	\multicolumn{11}{l}{\footnotesize $^\ddagger$Generator: Qwen2.5-7B (fp16); scorer: Qwen2.5-1.5B.}
32	\end{tabular}
33	\end{table*}
34	
35	\begin{figure}[t]
36	\centering
37	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_auc_decay.pdf}
38	\caption{Pairwise $\auc$ decay across depth pairs for model-mode configurations (solid) and decoding strategies (dashed). The horizontal dashed line marks $\theta = 0.60$.}
39	\label{fig:auc_decay}
40	\end{figure}
41	
42	Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} and Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay} show a consistent pattern: 0v1 discrimination is near-perfect ($\auc \geq 0.96$), followed by a sharp drop at 1v2 ($\auc$: 0.6112--0.6955), with 2v3 falling below $\theta$ (0.5492--0.5893) and deeper pairs converging toward chance.
43	All five 1v2 point estimates exceed $\theta$, confirmed by bootstrap CIs (most marginal lower bound: Qwen-1.5B-continuation at 0.602); all five 2v3 point estimates and CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (permutation $p < 0.001$ for all boundary comparisons).
44	This establishes $\Kempirical = 2$ as consistent across all 10 tested conditions (6 independent model-mode configurations and 4 decoding-strategy ablation variants on the Qwen-rewrite configuration; Table~\ref{tab:s2_decoding}).
45	Under cross-model scoring, Qwen-continuation $\Kempirical$ drops to 1 (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), indicating a model-specific component in the most marginal 1v2 boundary signal.
46	The sharp step-function pattern reflects the concentration of information loss: human text exhibits heavy-tailed, bursty surprisal patterns that are substantially altered by even a single autoregressive pass.
47	Subsequent generations operate on already-smoothed distributions, yielding progressively smaller marginal changes that fall below detectability within two steps.
48	
49	The 1v2 $\auc$ varies across models: Qwen-rewrite (0.6955) $>$ Pythia (0.6539) $>$ OLMo (0.6145) $\approx$ Qwen-continuation (0.6112).
50	The spread due to generation mode within a single model ($\Delta = 8.4$\,pp) exceeds the spread across models in the same mode ($\Delta = 3.9$\,pp), suggesting that generation mode appears to have a larger effect than model architecture, though formal interaction testing is beyond our current scope.
51	
52	\paragraph{Cross-scale validation.}
53	Qwen2.5-7B in continuation mode (scored by Qwen2.5-1.5B) confirms $\Kempirical = 2$: 1v2 $\auc = 0.6168$ $[0.608,\,0.626]$ (CI lower bound $> \theta$), 2v3 $\auc = 0.5492$ $[0.539,\,0.559]$ (Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci}).
54	The 0v1 $\auc$ drops to 0.9638 (${\sim}$3\,pp below ${\leq}$1.5B models), consistent with larger models generating more human-like text; yet the $\Kempirical$ boundary remains unchanged, extending the invariance from 1.5B to 7B.
55	
56	\paragraph{Base-vs.-instruct ablation.}
57	Qwen2.5-1.5B (base) in continuation mode yields $\Kempirical = 2$: 0v1 $\auc = 0.987$, 1v2 $\auc = 0.626$, 2v3 $\auc = 0.550$ (Table~\ref{tab:setup}).
58	The 0v1 signal is slightly lower than the matched Instruct model ($0.987$ vs.\ $0.997$), consistent with base models producing less stylistically divergent text, but $\Kempirical$ is identical, confirming that the depth boundary is not an instruction-tuning artifact.
59	
60	\begin{figure}[t]
61	\centering
62	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_kstar_theta.pdf}
63	\caption{$\Kempirical$ as a function of $\theta$ across six model-mode configurations, computed using the 95\% CI lower bound criterion (Eq.~\ref{eq:kstar}). The dashed line marks the operational threshold $\theta{=}0.60$ used throughout, where all configurations yield $\Kempirical{=}2$. Qwen-rewrite yields the highest $\Kempirical$ at all $\theta$; at $\theta{=}0.70$, $\Kempirical{=}1$ universally.}
64	\label{fig:kstar_theta}
65	\end{figure}
66	
67	Figure~\ref{fig:kstar_theta} shows $\Kempirical$ as a function of $\theta$ (conservative CI-lower-bound variant): unanimous $\Kempirical = 2$ holds within $\theta \in [0.580, 0.600]$.
68	At $\theta = 0.55$, $\Kempirical = 3$ for Qwen-rewrite and Qwen-continuation while Pythia, OLMo, and Qwen-7B remain at $\Kempirical = 2$; at $\theta = 0.65$, all continuation modes drop to $\Kempirical = 1$ while rewrite retains $\Kempirical = 2$; at $\theta = 0.70$, $\Kempirical = 1$ universally.
69	All four decoding configurations (greedy, nucleus $p{=}0.9$, $T{=}0.70$, $T{=}1.2$) likewise yield $\Kempirical = 2$ at $\theta = 0.60$, with 1v2 $\auc$ in $[0.6866, 0.7039]$ (bootstrap CI lower bounds $\geq 0.677$, all ${>}\theta$; Table~\ref{tab:s2_decoding}).
70	Bootstrap CIs confirm 2v3 upper bounds below $\theta$ for 3/4 decoding variants; the nucleus $p{=}0.9$ condition (2v3 $\auc = 0.5917$, CI $[0.582, 0.601]$) has its upper bound marginally straddling $\theta$ by 0.001, consistent with measurement noise.
71	
72	%% ====================================================================
73	\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer}
74	\label{sec:transfer}
75	
76	\begin{figure}[t]
77	\centering
78	\includegraphics[width=0.85\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_transfer_heatmap.pdf}
79	\caption{Cross-model transfer heatmap (6-class ordinal accuracy). Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo achieves 90--92\% retention; Qwen-rewrite$\to$continuation-mode models: 61--63\%.}
80	\label{fig:transfer_heatmap}
81	\end{figure}
82	
83	The universality of $\Kempirical = 2$ raises a natural question: does the depth boundary reflect properties of the text itself, or generator-specific artifacts?
84	Cross-model transfer experiments address this directly.
85	
86	Figure~\ref{fig:transfer_heatmap} shows the transfer accuracy matrix (full matrix in Table~\ref{tab:s1_transfer}).
87	Continuation-mode transfer is high: Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo retains 90--92\% of within-model accuracy, Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$Pythia 84--85\%, and Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$OLMo 80--85\%.
88	At the 0v1 boundary, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 for all pairs (range: 0.963--0.991).
89	These retention rates suggest that depth features transfer across generators when computed by a fixed scorer.
90	The high retention indicates that the relative importance of depth features is encoded in distributional text properties---surprisal variance, lexical diversity---rather than in generator-specific fingerprints, enabling generator-agnostic deployment when a consistent scorer is used.
91	
92	Qwen-rewrite classifiers transfer poorly (61--63\% retention to Pythia/OLMo), confirming reliance on mode-specific artifacts.
93	Cross-mode transfer is asymmetric: continuation$\to$rewrite retains 89\% while rewrite$\to$continuation retains 82\%, indicating that continuation-mode features form a generalizable subset.
94	
95	\paragraph{Cross-scorer validation.}
96	To test whether depth signals depend on the scorer model, we replace the Qwen self-scorer with two alternative scorers (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B) for feature extraction on Qwen-generated text.
97	Feature rankings remain highly correlated across all scorer pairs (Spearman $\rho > 0.90$), confirming that feature ordering is text-intrinsic.
98	Absolute discriminability, however, is scorer-sensitive at the $\Kempirical$ boundary.
99	For Qwen-rewrite, $\Kempirical = 2$ is scorer-invariant: 1v2 $\auc$ remains stable under cross-scoring (Pythia: 0.7012, OLMo: 0.6947; self-scorer baseline: 0.6955; Table~\ref{tab:crossscorer}).
100	For Qwen-continuation---already the most marginal self-scorer condition (CI lower bound exceeds $\theta$ by only 0.2\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci})---$\Kempirical$ drops from 2 to 1 under both alternative scorers (1v2 $\auc$: $0.6112 \to 0.5923$ [Pythia], $0.5858$ [OLMo], both below $\theta$).
101	This dissociation---scorer-invariant feature rankings but scorer-sensitive boundary classification---indicates that cross-scoring preserves the relative importance structure of depth features while attenuating the absolute signal, with consequences only where the self-scorer margin is already thin.
102	Crucially, both alternative scorers agree on $\Kempirical$ for each generation mode ($\Kempirical = 2$ for rewrite, $1$ for continuation), indicating that $\Kempirical$ is determined by the generation process rather than the choice of scoring model.

169	\subsection{Binary Detector Confidence and Depth}
170	\label{sec:binary_confidence}
171	
172	A natural question is whether binary detector confidence---even without ordinal training---implicitly encodes depth information.
173	We evaluate DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye} (log-PPL) and Binoculars~\cite{hans2024binoculars} (cross-model PPL ratio; observer: Pythia-1.4B, performer: OLMo-1B) across all four model-mode configurations, reporting both Spearman $\rho$ with true depth and 6-class depth classification accuracy.
174	
175	Moderate rank correlations exist ($|\rho| = 0.06$--$0.46$; Table~\ref{tab:s9_binary_spearman}), but these do not translate to practical depth discrimination: binary detectors effectively separate human from machine text (0v1 $\auc$: 0.54--0.85, depending on observer-generator matching), but confidence scores collapse to noise for depths $\geq 1$.
176	Six-class accuracy confirms this: most configurations fall at or below the random baseline of 0.167; only Qwen-rewrite (0.199) and Qwen-continuation (0.183) marginally exceed it, while Pythia (0.130) and OLMo (0.127) fall below.
177	Pairwise $\auc$ yields $\Kempirical^{\text{binary}} \leq 1$ for most detector--generator pairs: all pairs $\geq$1v2 fall to 0.50--0.60, well below the OBD-15D baseline (0v1 $> 0.99$, 1v2: 0.61--0.70, $\Kempirical = 2$).
178	Multiple conditions exhibit non-monotonic AUC at deeper pairs (e.g., 2v3 $<$ 3v4 $<$ 4v5 for Qwen-continuation), violating the monotonic ordering required for depth interpretation.
179	The observed rank correlation is thus an artifact of 0v1 separation rather than fine-grained depth signal.
180

1	\section{Application: $\Kstar$-Aware Data Filtering}
2	\label{sec:filtering}
3	
4	$\Kempirical = 2$ makes a falsifiable prediction: binary curation should suffice, and graduated performance should converge toward binary as the decay steepness increases.
5	We compare six strategies on 30{,}000 documents (depths 0--5): (i)~\textbf{no-filter}, (ii)~\textbf{binary-ours} ($w = 1 - P(\text{synthetic})$ from 15D LightGBM), (iii)~\textbf{binary-Drayson}~\citep{drayson2025}, (iv)~\textbf{graduated} ($w = \exp(-\alpha \cdot \hat{d})$, $\alpha \in \{0.1,\ldots,0.9\}$), (v)~\textbf{surprisal} (retain above median), and (vi)~\textbf{DSIR}~\citep{xie2023dsir}.
6	We fine-tune Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via LoRA (rank~8, $\alpha_{\text{LoRA}}{=}16$) for 3 epochs on MMLU and HellaSwag across 5 seeds (51 total runs; this 100\% synthetic setting is an upper bound~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}).
7

9	\centering
10	\small
11	\caption{Downstream filtering performance (5 seeds). Full $\alpha$ sweep and significance tests in Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}.}
12	\label{tab:tab_filtering_main}
13	\input{tables/tab_filtering_main}

16	Binary-ours minimizes MMLU degradation most effectively (Table~\ref{tab:tab_filtering_main}), reducing the gap from $-$1.53\,pp (no-filter) to $-$0.77\,pp (${\sim}$50\% reduction; $p_{\text{corr}} < 0.05$ vs.\ all alternatives).
17	These effects are measured in a 100\% synthetic upper-bound setting; real-world contamination ratios are typically lower, and effect sizes would scale accordingly.
18	The strategy ordering is interpretable through $\Kempirical$: binary filtering exploits the one reliable boundary (0v1), while graduated strategies assign weights to depths 2--5 based on near-random classifier outputs, injecting noise.
19	Graduated filtering converges monotonically toward binary: at $\alpha{=}0.9$, it matches binary-ours on HellaSwag exactly ($\Delta = 0$, $p_{\text{corr}} = 1.00$) but remains significantly worse on MMLU ($p_{\text{corr}} = 0.011$).
20	DSIR is indistinguishable from no-filter, confirming that depth-aware features are necessary for curation in recursively contaminated corpora (Figure~\ref{fig:filtering_strategies} in Appendix).

# 论文图表方案

> 项目：gen-depth-contamination
> 目标投稿：EMNLP ARR May 25, 2026
> 最后更新：2026-05-12

---

## Fig 1: Method Overview / Pipeline 图

**类型**：示意图 / flow diagram

**数据来源**：无数据依赖，纯概念图

**核心信息**：一图看懂整个方法——从人类文本出发，经过递归 LLM 生成形成不同 depth 的文本，提取统计特征后送入 ordinal depth classifier，最终输出 depth 估计用于 graduated filtering。读者看完应理解 (1) depth chain 的构造方式 (2) 特征提取到分类的 pipeline (3) graduated filtering 的思路。

**设计要点**：

- **布局**：左到右水平流程，分三个区域——Corpus Construction / Feature Extraction / Depth-Aware Curation
- **Corpus Construction 区域**：
  - 左起一个 Human Text 方块（X₀），颜色最深（深蓝 #1a5276）
  - 依次经过 LLM 信道符号（▷）连接到 X₁, X₂, ..., X₅
  - 每个 Xₖ 用渐变色编码 depth：depth 0 深蓝 → depth 5 浅蓝/白色，隐喻信息衰减
  - X₀ 到 X₅ 之间画一条从粗到细的灰色箭头，底部标注 "I(X₀; Xₖ) ↓ (DPI)"
- **Feature Extraction 区域**：
  - 三组特征用图标 + 颜色区分：Surprisal (蓝 #2980b9) / Diversity (绿 #27ae60) / Tail-thinning (橙 #e67e22)
  - 简洁的 15-dim feature vector 示意
- **Depth-Aware Curation 区域**：
  - Ordinal Classifier 输出 depth 估计 k̂
  - 底部分支：graduated weight = quality(k̂)/quality(0) → 加权训练数据
  - 与 binary filtering（remove all synthetic）对比的小示意
- **底部信息条**：DPI 理论支撑——"Data Processing Inequality: information about X₀ can only decrease with depth"
- **字体**：标题用 sans-serif bold，标注用 9pt，数学符号用 LaTeX 渲染
- **配色**：以蓝色系为主色调，三组特征颜色贯穿后续所有图表

**制作工具**：TikZ（LaTeX 原生，与论文排版一致，方便调整尺寸）。如时间不够，matplotlib + 手动布局。

---

## Fig 2: Pairwise AUC 随 depth 衰减曲线（核心结果图）

**类型**：折线图

**数据来源**：
- P0-9 (全配置特征提取) + P0-10 (LightGBM 5-fold CV)
- 文件：`artifacts/analysis/pairwise_auc_matrix.csv`
- 每个 (model, decoding_strategy) 配置的 pairwise AUC 值

**核心信息**：depth signal 存在且随深度单调衰减，K* 可精确测量。不同模型/解码策略的衰减速度不同但趋势一致。读者看完应得出：(1) depth 0v1 区分度最高 (2) 衰减是单调的 (3) K* 位置清晰可读。

**设计要点**：

- **X 轴**：depth pair (0v1, 1v2, 2v3, 3v4, 4v5)，等间距
- **Y 轴**：AUC，范围 [0.45, 1.0]，0.5 处标注 "random baseline"
- **线条**：
  - 主实验线（Qwen2.5-1.5B × 5 种解码策略）：实线，不同明度的蓝色系
    - D-greedy: 深蓝实线 ●
    - D-p90: 蓝色实线 ■
    - D-p95: 中蓝实线 ▲（MVP 配置，加粗）
    - D-lowT: 浅蓝实线 ◆
    - D-highT: 天蓝实线 ★
  - 跨模型线：虚线
    - Pythia-1.4B (D-p95): 红色虚线 ●
    - OLMo-1B (D-p95): 绿色虚线 ■
    - Qwen2.5-7B (D-p95): 紫色虚线 ▲
- **水平参考线**：AUC=0.60 灰色虚线，右侧标注 "K* threshold"
- **K* 标注**：每条曲线与 0.60 线交叉处用竖向箭头标注 K* 值（如 K*=3）
- **误差带**：5-fold CV 的 ±1 std 用半透明色带
- **图例**：右侧或图下方，按模型分组

**制作工具**：matplotlib (seaborn style)。代码模板在 `draw-paper-figure` skill 中。

---

## Fig 3: JSD 衰减曲线 + 理论预测叠加

**类型**：折线图（双 panel 或叠加）

**数据来源**：
- P0-9 特征提取中的 JSD 计算：`artifacts/analysis/jsd_decay.csv`
- 每个配置下 JSD(P_{X_0}, P_{X_k}) 对 k 的值
- 理论预测：Proposition 2 的 ρ^k · d(P_{X_0}, P*) 指数衰减 bound

**核心信息**：实验观测的 JSD 衰减与信道级联理论（DPI bound）定性一致。指数衰减拟合 vs 多项式衰减拟合的 AIC/BIC 对比验证 Proposition 3 的经验假设。读者看完应得出：(1) MI 确实单调衰减 (2) 衰减速率与解码策略相关 (3) 理论框架有实验支撑。

**设计要点**：

- **Panel A — JSD 衰减观测**：
  - X 轴：depth k (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
  - Y 轴：JSD(P_{X_0}, P_{X_k})，对数刻度可选
  - 多条实线：不同 decoding strategies（复用 Fig 2 配色）
  - 叠加虚线：指数拟合 ρ̂^k · C（用 least squares fit）
  - 标注拟合的 ρ̂ 值和 R² 或 AIC
- **Panel B — 衰减模型对比**：
  - 分组柱状图或表格嵌入
  - X 轴：decoding strategy
  - Y 轴：AIC（越低越好）
  - 两组柱：exponential fit / polynomial fit
  - 颜色：exponential 蓝色 / polynomial 橙色
  - 核心观察：greedy 更符合指数衰减，high-T 可能更接近多项式
- **辅助元素**：
  - Panel A 中用灰色水平带标注 "noise floor"（JSD 值低于此不可靠）
  - 箭头标注 convergence to P*
- **配色**：与 Fig 2 一致

**制作工具**：matplotlib，subplot(1,2) 布局

---

## Fig 4: Feature Importance Ranking

**类型**：水平柱状图

**数据来源**：
- P0-10 LightGBM classifier 的 feature importance (gain-based)
- 文件：`artifacts/analysis/feature_importance.csv`
- 15 维特征的 importance 排序

**核心信息**：哪类特征最 depth-discriminative。读者看完应得出：(1) 三组特征的相对重要性排序 (2) 单个最重要特征是什么 (3) 不同特征组的贡献是互补的还是冗余的。

**设计要点**：

- **布局**：水平柱状图，特征名在 Y 轴，importance 在 X 轴
- **排序**：按 importance 降序（最重要的在最上方）
- **颜色编码（贯穿全文）**：
  - Surprisal 组 (9 维): 蓝色系 #2980b9
  - Diversity 组 (3 维): 绿色系 #27ae60
  - Tail-thinning 组 (3 维): 橙色系 #e67e22
- **特征名标注**：
  - 简写 + 全称 tooltip（如 "surp_mean" / "mean token surprisal"）
  - 同组特征用括号分组标注
- **分组分隔线**：在不同颜色组之间用细灰线分隔（如果特征交错排列则不需要）
- **误差条**：5-fold CV 的 importance std
- **右侧标注**：每组特征的累计 importance 百分比
- **图例**：右上角，三色块 + 组名

**制作工具**：matplotlib (barh)

---

## Fig 5: Graduated vs Binary Filtering 下游对比

**类型**：分组柱状图

**数据来源**：
- P0-12 下游过滤评估结果
- 文件：`artifacts/downstream/filtering_comparison.csv`
- 4 种过滤策略 × 下游 benchmark 分数

**核心信息**：graduated filtering 优于 binary filtering 和 no filtering。读者看完应得出：(1) 过滤好于不过滤 (2) graduated > binary (3) 差异具有统计显著性。

**设计要点**：

- **X 轴**：filtering 策略，4 组
  - No filter (灰色)
  - Binary (DivEye) (红色)
  - Graduated (本文方法) (蓝色，加粗边框突出)
  - Surplexity (紫色)
- **Y 轴**：Accuracy (%)
- **Panel 布局**：subplot(1,2) 或 subplot(1,3)
  - Panel A: MMLU (5-shot)
  - Panel B: HellaSwag (10-shot)
  - Panel C: XSum ROUGE-L（如果 P1-7 完成）
- **误差条**：bootstrap 95% CI
- **显著性标注**：
  - graduated vs binary: 横线 + * 或 ** 标注 p-value
  - graduated vs no-filter: 同上
- **数值标注**：每个柱顶标注精确值（如 "43.2"）
- **baseline 参考线**：no-filter 的值用灰色水平虚线贯穿
- **如果有多个污染比例**（P1-2 完成时）：
  - 改为 subplot(2,2) 或 subplot(1,3)，每个 panel 一个污染比例
  - 或改为折线图：X 轴=污染比例 (10%/30%/50%), 多条线=不同策略

**制作工具**：matplotlib (bar + errorbar)

---

## Fig 6: Feature Group × Depth 判别力热力图（降解序分析）

**类型**：热力图

**数据来源**：
- P0-11 K* + 饱和边界分析
- 文件：`artifacts/analysis/feature_group_saturation.csv`
- 每个 feature group 在每个 depth pair 上的 AUC

**核心信息**：揭示 "linguistic degradation ordering"——不同语言维度在哪个 depth 率先丧失判别力。读者看完应得出：(1) 哪组特征最先饱和 (2) 哪组特征最晚饱和（最 robust）(3) 饱和顺序是否跨模型一致。

**设计要点**：

- **行**：Feature group（Surprisal / Diversity / Tail-thinning），每组可进一步拆分单特征

**类型**：表格

**数据来源**：
- P0-10 所有配置的 pairwise AUC
- 文件：`artifacts/analysis/pairwise_auc_matrix.csv`

**核心信息**：跨模型 × 跨解码策略的 K* 一致性或差异。读者看完应得出：(1) 每个配置的 K* 是多少 (2) K* 在哪些条件下变化 (3) 整体结论的可靠性。

**设计要点**：

- **布局**：Ridge plot（垂直堆叠，从上到下 depth 0→5）
- **X 轴**：mean token surprisal（或 mean log-prob 取负）
- **Y 轴**：密度（每个 depth 一条分布曲线）
- **颜色**：与全文 depth 色标一致（深蓝→浅蓝）

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When models train on the outputs of earlier models, the resulting multi-generational synthetic text degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively generating from previous outputs without retraining); we study the latter, which isolates generation-level information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically, discarding the generational depth dimension.

The gap cuts across three communities.
Binary detection methods~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate, and their confidence scores fail to discriminate beyond the binary boundary (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}).
Data contamination detection via membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question (whether specific texts appeared in training data) and likewise provides no depth signal.
The model collapse literature~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, schaeffer2025position} characterizes recursive degradation at the macro level but provides no per-text depth estimation tool.
Data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} ignore recursive depth.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone, nor quantifies the boundary beyond which such estimation becomes infeasible.

The Data Processing Inequality guarantees that information degrades monotonically across generations, motivating a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$.
We empirically measure $\Kempirical$---the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations---using 15 statistical features and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the bootstrap 95\% CI for pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$.

Our contributions center on two empirical findings:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{$\Kempirical = 2$ at $\theta{=}0.60$} (Cohen's $h{\approx}0.20$) across 6 model configurations (1B--7B, base and instruct) and 4 decoding strategies, with all 1v2 CI lower bounds exceeding $\theta$ and all 2v3 CI upper bounds below $\theta$ ($p \leq 0.002$; Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).
  Generation mode appears to have a larger effect than model architecture ($+$8.4\,pp rewrite vs.\ continuation within Qwen; $3.9$\,pp spread across continuation-mode models), though formal interaction testing is beyond our current scope.
  This is independently corroborated: both supervised OBD and zero-shot frontier LLMs fail comparably at depths $\geq 2$ (McNemar $p > 0.05$), providing converging evidence consistent with $\Kempirical{=}2$ reflecting a data-intrinsic boundary (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
  \item \textbf{Model-free cross-model transfer}: 15 statistical features enable 80--92\% accuracy retention across continuation-mode generators with scorer-invariant feature ordering ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), with surprisal-variance features dominating ($\rho \geq 0.85$).
  Cross-scorer validation confirms that $\Kempirical$ is governed by the generation process rather than the scoring model.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent As a downstream validation, $\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts the strategy ordering in data filtering: binary curation at the $\Kempirical$ boundary minimizes degradation most effectively (MMLU $0.5941$ vs.\ base $0.6018$), while graduated ($0.5892$) and surprisal-based ($0.5894$) strategies provide no additional benefit (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	\subsection{The One-Wash Laundering Effect}
5	\label{sec:why_kstar}
6	\label{sec:one_wash}
7	
8	The shallowness of $\Kempirical = 2$ reflects the concentration of information loss: the 0v1 boundary is near-trivially separable ($\auc \geq 0.96$), 1v2 drops by ${\sim}$30\,pp, and 2v3 falls below $\theta$---the generation operator acts as a lossy channel with diminishing marginal information loss.
9	Consistency across four decoding strategies (Table~\ref{tab:s2_decoding}) reinforces that $\Kempirical$ is governed by the generation process rather than the sampling algorithm.
10	Even at the most marginal 1v2 condition (Qwen-continuation, CI lower bound exceeds $\theta$ by only 0.2\,pp), $\Kempirical = 2$ survives under self-scoring; on the 2v3 side, CI upper bounds confirm non-discrimination in 9/10 conditions, with the single borderline case (nucleus $p{=}0.9$, CI upper${} = 0.601$) consistent with measurement noise at near-threshold values.
11	Cross-scale validation at 7B (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}) extends this from 1.5B to 7B despite reduced 0v1 signal ($0.9638$ vs.\ $> 0.99$).
12	
13	The practical consequence is a three-tier taxonomy: human-authored (depth~0), first-generation synthetic (depth~1), and deeper synthetic (depth~$\geq 2$).
14	A single generation pass suffices to render text statistically indistinguishable from multiply recycled content---a \emph{one-wash laundering} effect that limits depth-aware corpus curation to a binary boundary.
15	This connects to model collapse: Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} observed that tail-distribution degradation is most acute in the earliest generations; our prompt-chain results show an analogous per-text pattern.
16	
17	Per-depth analysis provides the most direct evidence that this boundary is not methodological.
18	OBD achieves 96\% depth-0 recall but only 14--22\% for depths 2--4; frontier LLMs show 69--77\% depth-0 recall and 8--38\% for depths 2--4 (McNemar $p > 0.05$ vs.\ OBD; Table~\ref{tab:s3_llm_zeroshot}).
19	This convergence across fundamentally different approaches---supervised statistical classification and zero-shot frontier LLMs---provides converging evidence that the saturation reflects a data-intrinsic boundary rather than a method limitation.
20	Binary detector confidence corroborates: despite moderate Spearman correlations ($|\rho|$ up to 0.46), 6-class accuracy is at or below chance ($\leq 0.199$ vs.\ 0.167 baseline), and Qwen-rewrite exhibits a sign reversal ($\rho > 0$), disqualifying confidence as a reliable depth proxy.
21	
22	\subsection{Why Graduated Filtering Fails}
23	\label{sec:negative_graduated}
24	
25	Since 2v3 $\auc < \theta$ for all configurations, depth assignments for $d \geq 2$ approximate random labels; graduated weighting injects noise into importance weights, explaining the monotonic improvement with $\alpha$ as it converges toward binary thresholding (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
26	DSIR fails for a different reason---bigram feature hashing captures domain shift but not depth-correlated distributional signatures.
27	
28	\subsection{Representation Dependence of the Boundary}
29	\label{sec:repr_dependence}
30	
31	$\Kempirical$ is representation-dependent: frozen Qwen embeddings yield $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$, while Pythia and OLMo match the 15D boundary at $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 2$ (Table~\ref{tab:neural_probe_crossmodel}).
32	The hierarchy $\Kempirical^{15\text{D}}{=}2 < \Kempirical^{\text{neural}} \in \{2,3\}$ reflects an interpretability--sensitivity tradeoff: learned representations recover additional depth signal sufficient to push $\Kempirical$ to 3 for one model (Qwen), but this gain is model-dependent---the 15D features trade one depth level of sensitivity for cross-model universality (10/10 conditions $\Kempirical{=}2$, 3/3 models identical), making them the preferred operational choice.
33	Cross-scorer validation reinforces this: alternative scorers preserve feature rankings ($\rho > 0.90$) but reduce the marginal Qwen-continuation boundary from $\Kempirical = 2$ to 1, while rewrite-mode $\Kempirical = 2$ is preserved---$\Kempirical$ is governed by the generation operator rather than the scoring model.
34	A base-vs.-instruct ablation at 1.5B confirms $\Kempirical{=}2$ is independent of instruction tuning (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).
35	A potential length confound is also ruled out: in continuation mode the generation prompt is discarded so all depths $\geq 1$ are purely machine-generated, token counts are stable within depths 1--5 ($\leq$ 6-token range), and the length asymmetry (depth~0 ${\sim}$191 vs.\ depth~1+ 193--256 tokens) makes 0v1 detection more conservative, not inflated (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
36	\label{sec:length_confound}

1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\begin{figure*}[t]
5	\centering
6	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
7	\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
8	\label{fig:pipeline}
9	\end{figure*}
10	
11	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
12	\label{sec:formulation}
13	
14	A generation operator $G_\delta$ (LLM + decoding strategy $\delta$) produces successive generations $X \to Y_1 \to \cdots \to Y_K$, where $Y_k = G_\delta(Y_{k-1})$ and $Y_0 \triangleq X$ (Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
15	This sequence forms a Markov chain.
16	By the Data Processing Inequality, $I(X; Y_1) \geq I(X; Y_2) \geq \cdots \geq 0$: the original signal degrades monotonically.
17	Together with Markov chain convergence, this guarantees a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations are indistinguishable.
18	
19	We define the operational lower bound:
20	\begin{equation}
21	  \Kempirical = \max\{k \geq 1 : \auc_{k-1,k} > \theta\},
22	  \label{eq:kstar}
23	\end{equation}
24	where $\auc_{k-1,k}$ is the point-estimate pairwise AUC and $\theta = 0.60$ corresponds to Cohen's $h \approx 0.20$\footnote{$h = 2\arcsin\!\sqrt{0.60} - 2\arcsin\!\sqrt{0.50} \approx 0.2014$, a ``small'' effect size by Cohen's (1988) convention.} (a conventional small-effect-size threshold), well above the permutation null (95th percentile $< 0.55$).
25	Bootstrap 95\% CIs (1{,}000 resamples) provide uncertainty quantification: we verify that boundary-pair CI lower bounds exceed $\theta$ and non-boundary-pair CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$ (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).
26	$\theta{=}0.60$ is justified independently by Cohen's $h \approx 0.20$ and a 10K permutation test ($p < 0.002$); the filtering evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) uses the OBD classifier as-is rather than re-optimizing $\theta$, avoiding circularity.
27	$\Kempirical$ varies with $\theta$: at $\theta{=}0.55$, $\Kempirical{=}2$--$3$ depending on configuration ($\Kempirical{=}3$ for Qwen variants, $\Kempirical{=}2$ for Pythia and OLMo); at $\theta{=}0.65$, continuation modes drop to $\Kempirical{=}1$; at $\theta{=}0.70$, $\Kempirical{=}1$ universally (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}).
28	
29	\subsection{Features and Classifier}
30	\label{sec:features}
31	
32	Each document is characterized by a 15-dimensional feature vector spanning four groups: \emph{surprisal moments} (mean, std, skewness, kurtosis; 4~dims), \emph{surprisal derivatives} (mean and std of first- and second-order differences, plus first-order skewness; 5~dims), \emph{vocabulary diversity} (type-token ratio, hapax legomena ratio, self-BLEU; 3~dims), and \emph{frequency tail statistics} (frequency kurtosis, entropy, rare token fraction; 3~dims).
33	All features are computed from token-level surprisal values via an external scorer model (full definitions in Table~\ref{tab:s5_features}, Appendix).
34	Self-BLEU is computed within each CV fold using only same-fold, same-depth reference samples to prevent leakage; it ranks \#1 in 1/8 conditions (greedy decoding) but is absent from the top-3 in all 7 others.
35	Removing self-BLEU reduces mean $\auc_{1v2}$ by $< 1$\,pp across all models (14D $\Kempirical = 2$ for all 4 configurations); in deployment where depth labels are unavailable, self-BLEU can be replaced with corpus-level self-similarity or omitted with minimal performance loss.
36	Hand-crafted features enable cross-generator transfer without retraining and permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties.
37	
38	We use \emph{Ordinal Binary Decomposition} (OBD), decomposing the $(K{+}1)$-class problem into $K$ cumulative binary sub-classifiers, each estimating $P(\text{depth} > k \mid \mathbf{x})$ via LightGBM (hyperparameters in Table~\ref{tab:s6_lgbm_params}).
39	OBD achieves lower MAE than multiclass LightGBM (e.g., 0.984 vs.\ 1.016 on Qwen-rewrite) while maintaining superior pairwise $\auc$ (mean 0.6095 vs.\ 0.4883 for ordinal logistic regression).
40	
41	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
42	\label{sec:experimental_setup}
43	
44	We evaluate six configurations spanning three model families (Table~\ref{tab:setup}): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (rewrite and continuation modes), Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, continuation), Qwen2.5-7B (continuation), Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B (continuation).
45	Each uses 5{,}000 C4 seeds truncated to 256 tokens, recursively generated for $K{=}5$ iterations (30{,}000 documents per configuration).
46	Default decoding: nucleus $p{=}0.95$, $T{=}1.0$; decoding ablation covers greedy, $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$.
47	Continuation mode truncates seeds to 128 tokens and extends to 256; rewrite mode paraphrases the full text.
48	Evaluation: 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by seed document; pairwise $\auc$ as primary metric.
49

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We presented the first systematic measurement of the generational depth discrimination boundary $\Kempirical$ for recursive synthetic text.
5	Two primary findings emerge:
6	(a)~$\Kempirical = 2$ at $\theta{=}0.60$ (Cohen's $h{\approx}0.20$), consistent across all tested configurations from 1B to 7B under self-scoring ($p \leq 0.002$; most marginal: 0.2\,pp above $\theta$), implying a one-wash laundering effect.
7	Convergent failure of both supervised classifiers and frontier LLMs at depths $\geq 2$ (McNemar $p > 0.05$) provides converging evidence consistent with this reflecting a data-intrinsic boundary rather than a method limitation.
8	Generation mode appears to have a larger effect than model architecture ($\Delta = 8.4$\,pp), but rewrite-mode advantages are non-transferable (61--63\% vs.\ 80--92\%).
9	(b)~Model-free statistical features enable 80--92\% cross-model transfer retention among continuation-mode generators with scorer-invariant feature ordering ($\rho > 0.90$), with surprisal-variance features dominating across model families ($\rho \geq 0.85$); cross-scorer validation confirms that $\Kempirical$ is governed by the generation process rather than the scoring model, enabling depth estimation for text from unknown generators without retraining.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We presented the first systematic measurement of the generational depth discrimination boundary $\Kempirical$ for recursive synthetic text.
Two primary findings emerge:
(a)~$\Kempirical = 2$ at $\theta{=}0.60$ (Cohen's $h{\approx}0.20$), consistent across all tested configurations from 1B to 7B under self-scoring ($p \leq 0.002$; most marginal: 0.2\,pp above $\theta$), implying a one-wash laundering effect.
Convergent failure of both supervised classifiers and frontier LLMs at depths $\geq 2$ (McNemar $p > 0.05$) provides converging evidence consistent with this reflecting a data-intrinsic boundary rather than a method limitation.
Generation mode appears to have a larger effect than model architecture ($\Delta = 8.4$\,pp), but rewrite-mode advantages are non-transferable (61--63\% vs.\ 80--92\%).
(b)~Model-free statistical features enable 80--92\% cross-model transfer retention among continuation-mode generators with scorer-invariant feature ordering ($\rho > 0.90$), with surprisal-variance features dominating across model families ($\rho \geq 0.85$); cross-scorer validation confirms that $\Kempirical$ is governed by the generation process rather than the scoring model, enabling depth estimation for text from unknown generators without retraining.
As a downstream validation, $\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts the optimal curation granularity: binary filtering minimizes degradation most effectively; finer ordinal structure and depth-agnostic methods (DSIR) provide no benefit.

Future work includes scaling beyond 7B, extending to naturalistic multi-domain corpora, and developing model-agnostic neural probes.
Our prompt-chain protocol isolates generation-level information loss in a controlled setting; establishing the retrain-chain $\Kstar$ relationship, where training dynamics introduce additional degradation, is a natural next step.
The 100\% synthetic filtering experiment characterizes an upper bound; mixed-corpus dose-response studies remain open.
Our base-vs.-instruct ablation confirms $\Kempirical{=}2$ is independent of instruction tuning, though broader architecture variation warrants further investigation.

"""

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ARTIFACT_DIR = ROOT / "artifacts"
JSON_PATH = ARTIFACT_DIR / "exp003_analysis.json"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FALLBACK_AUC = {
    "Config1-Greedy":  {"0v1": 0.9797, "1v2": 0.6893, "2v3": 0.5613, "3v4": 0.5404, "4v5": 0.5139},
    "Config2-Nuc09":   {"0v1": 0.9946, "1v2": 0.6866, "2v3": 0.5917, "3v4": 0.5466, "4v5": 0.5068},
    "Config3-T07":     {"0v1": 0.9878, "1v2": 0.6887, "2v3": 0.5902, "3v4": 0.5393, "4v5": 0.5349},
    "Config4-T12":     {"0v1": 0.9982, "1v2": 0.7039, "2v3": 0.5823, "3v4": 0.5293, "4v5": 0.5237},
}

CONFIG_LABELS = {
    "Config1-Greedy": "Greedy",
    "Config2-Nuc09":  "Nuc p=.9, T=1.0",
    "Config3-T07":    "Nuc p=.95, T=0.7",
    "Config4-T12":    "Nuc p=.95, T=1.2",
}

DEPTH_PAIRS = ["0v1", "1v2", "2v3", "3v4", "4v5"]
DEPTH_LABELS = ["0 vs 1", "1 vs 2", "2 vs 3", "3 vs 4", "4 vs 5"]

COLORS_FILL = ["#4E79A7", "#F28E2B", "#59A14F", "#E15759"]
COLORS_EDGE = ["#2B5A83", "#C06A10", "#3B7A32", "#B8393B"]

def load_data():
    if JSON_PATH.exists():
        with open(JSON_PATH) as f:
            blob = json.load(f)
        return blob.get("pairwise_auc_table", FALLBACK_AUC), blob
    return FALLBACK_AUC, {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def plot_grouped_bar(auc_table):
    plt.rcParams.update({
        "font.family": "serif",
        "font.serif": ["DejaVu Serif", "Times New Roman", "Computer Modern Roman"],
        "mathtext.fontset": "cm",
        "font.size": 8,
        "axes.titlesize": 9,
        "axes.labelsize": 8,
        "xtick.labelsize": 7,
        "ytick.labelsize": 7,
        "legend.fontsize": 6.5,
        "figure.dpi": 300,
        "savefig.dpi": 300,
        "savefig.bbox": "tight",
        "savefig.pad_inches": 0.02,
        "axes.spines.top": False,
        "axes.spines.right": False,
    })

    configs = list(auc_table.keys())
    n_configs = len(configs)
    n_pairs = len(DEPTH_PAIRS)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.5))

    bar_width = 0.18
    x = np.arange(n_pairs)

    for ci, cfg in enumerate(configs):
        vals = [auc_table[cfg].get(dp, float("nan")) for dp in DEPTH_PAIRS]
        offset = (ci - (n_configs - 1) / 2) * bar_width
        bars = ax.bar(
            x + offset, vals, bar_width,
            color=COLORS_FILL[ci], edgecolor=COLORS_EDGE[ci],
            linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.85,
            label=CONFIG_LABELS.get(cfg, cfg), zorder=3,
        )

    ax.axhline(0.60, color="#888888", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.7, zorder=2)
    ax.text(n_pairs - 0.5, 0.605, r"$\theta=0.60$", fontsize=6, color="#666666",
            ha="right", va="bottom")

    ax.axhline(0.50, color="#AAAAAA", linestyle=":", linewidth=0.6, zorder=2)
    ax.text(n_pairs - 0.5, 0.505, "chance", fontsize=5.5, color="#999999",
            ha="right", va="bottom")

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(DEPTH_LABELS)
    ax.set_xlabel("Depth pair")
    ax.set_ylabel("Pairwise AUC")
    ax.set_ylim(0.47, 1.03)

    ax.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, framealpha=0.9,
              edgecolor="#CCCCCC", fancybox=False, handlelength=1.2,
              handletextpad=0.4, borderpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.25)

    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    pdf_path = ARTIFACT_DIR / "exp003_decoding_ablation.pdf"
    png_path = ARTIFACT_DIR / "exp003_decoding_ablation.png"
    fig.savefig(pdf_path)
    fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"Saved: {pdf_path}")
    print(f"Saved: {png_path}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def print_and_save_table(auc_table, blob):
    top3 = blob.get("top3_features", {})
    theta_sens = blob.get("theta_sensitivity", {})

    header = f"{'Config':<22} {'Decoding':<22} {'1v2 AUC':>8} {'K*(θ=.60)':>10} {'Top-3 Features'}"
    sep = "-" * len(header)
    lines = [header, sep]

    decoding_map = {
        "Config1-Greedy": "greedy",
        "Config2-Nuc09":  "nucleus p=0.9, T=1.0",
        "Config3-T07":    "nucleus p=0.95, T=0.7",
        "Config4-T12":    "nucleus p=0.95, T=1.2",
    }

    tex_rows = []
    for cfg in auc_table:
        auc_1v2 = auc_table[cfg].get("1v2", float("nan"))
        kstar = theta_sens.get(cfg, {}).get("0.6", "—")
        feats = ", ".join(top3.get(cfg, []))
        dec = decoding_map.get(cfg, cfg)
        line = f"{cfg:<22} {dec:<22} {auc_1v2:>8.4f} {str(kstar):>10} {feats}"
        lines.append(line)
        tex_rows.append(
            f"  {cfg} & {dec} & {auc_1v2:.4f} & {kstar} & {feats} \\\\"
        )

    table_str = "\n".join(lines)
    print("\n" + table_str + "\n")

    tex = (
        "\\begin{table}[t]\n"
        "\\centering\n"
        "\\caption{Decoding ablation summary (exp-003). $K^*$ = max depth with AUC $>\\theta$.}\n"
        "\\label{tab:exp003-decoding}\n"
        "\\small\n"
        "\\begin{tabular}{llccc}\n"
        "\\toprule\n"
        "Config & Decoding & 1v2 AUC & $K^*(\\theta{=}0.60)$ & Top-3 Features \\\\\n"
        "\\midrule\n"
        + "\n".join(tex_rows) + "\n"
        "\\bottomrule\n"
        "\\end{tabular}\n"
        "\\end{table}\n"
    )

    tex_path = ARTIFACT_DIR / "exp003_decoding_ablation.tex"
    tex_path.write_text(tex)
    print(f"Saved: {tex_path}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    auc_table, blob = load_data()
    plot_grouped_bar(auc_table)
    print_and_save_table(auc_table, blob)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summary overview figure: pairwise AUC decay curves for all model-mode and decoding configs."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

# ── Data ──
data = {
    "Qwen-rewrite": {"0v1": 0.9956, "1v2": 0.6957, "2v3": 0.5893, "3v4": 0.5434, "4v5": 0.5343},
    "Pythia-cont":  {"0v1": 0.9932, "1v2": 0.6539, "2v3": 0.5514, "3v4": 0.5152, "4v5": 0.5136},
    "OLMo-cont":    {"0v1": 0.9970, "1v2": 0.6145, "2v3": 0.5496, "3v4": 0.5091, "4v5": 0.5045},
    "Qwen-cont":    {"0v1": 0.9972, "1v2": 0.6112, "2v3": 0.5609, "3v4": 0.5409, "4v5": 0.5141},
    "Greedy":       {"0v1": 0.9797, "1v2": 0.6893, "2v3": 0.5613, "3v4": 0.5404, "4v5": 0.5139},
    "Nuc p=0.9":    {"0v1": 0.9946, "1v2": 0.6866, "2v3": 0.5917, "3v4": 0.5466, "4v5": 0.5068},
    "T=0.7":        {"0v1": 0.9878, "1v2": 0.6887, "2v3": 0.5902, "3v4": 0.5393, "4v5": 0.5349},
    "T=1.2":        {"0v1": 0.9982, "1v2": 0.7039, "2v3": 0.5823, "3v4": 0.5293, "4v5": 0.5237},
}

x_labels = ["0 vs 1", "1 vs 2", "2 vs 3", "3 vs 4", "4 vs 5"]
x = np.arange(len(x_labels))

model_keys = ["Qwen-rewrite", "Pythia-cont", "OLMo-cont", "Qwen-cont"]
decode_keys = ["Greedy", "Nuc p=0.9", "T=0.7", "T=1.2"]

# Tableau 10 colorblind-safe subset
model_colors = ["#4e79a7", "#e15759", "#76b7b2", "#59a14f"]
decode_colors = ["#b07aa1", "#ff9da7", "#9c755f", "#bab0ac"]

# ── Style ──
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.size": 11,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.8,
    "xtick.major.width": 0.8,
    "ytick.major.width": 0.8,
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4), constrained_layout=True)

# K* boundary shading
ax.axvspan(0.5, 1.5, color="#fff9c4", alpha=0.55, zorder=0)
ax.text(1.0, 1.02, r"$K^*$ boundary", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9,
        fontstyle="italic", color="#8d6e00")

# Reference lines
ax.axhline(0.60, color="grey", ls="--", lw=0.8, zorder=1)
ax.text(4.55, 0.608, r"$\theta = 0.60$", fontsize=8.5, color="grey", va="bottom", ha="right")
ax.axhline(0.50, color="lightgrey", ls="--", lw=0.8, zorder=1)
ax.text(4.55, 0.508, "chance", fontsize=8.5, color="silver", va="bottom", ha="right")

# Plot model-mode curves (solid)
for key, color in zip(model_keys, model_colors):
    y = [data[key][k] for k in ["0v1", "1v2", "2v3", "3v4", "4v5"]]
    ax.plot(x, y, "-o", color=color, lw=1.8, markersize=5, label=key, zorder=3)

# Plot decoding curves (dashed)
for key, color in zip(decode_keys, decode_colors):
    y = [data[key][k] for k in ["0v1", "1v2", "2v3", "3v4", "4v5"]]
    ax.plot(x, y, "--o", color=color, lw=1.8, markersize=5, label=key, zorder=3)

# Axes
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(x_labels)
ax.set_xlabel("Depth Pair")
ax.set_ylabel("Pairwise AUC")
ax.set_ylim(0.45, 1.05)
ax.set_xlim(-0.25, 4.25)
ax.tick_params(direction="in")

# Legend – two groups
model_handles = [plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=c, lw=1.8, marker="o", markersize=4, label=k)
                 for k, c in zip(model_keys, model_colors)]
decode_handles = [plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=c, lw=1.8, ls="--", marker="o", markersize=4, label=k)
                  for k, c in zip(decode_keys, decode_colors)]

leg1 = ax.legend(handles=model_handles, title="Models", title_fontsize=9,
                 fontsize=8.5, loc="upper right", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.98),
                 framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="0.8")
ax.add_artist(leg1)
ax.legend(handles=decode_handles, title="Decoding", title_fontsize=9,
          fontsize=8.5, loc="center right", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.58),
          framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="0.8")

# ── Save ──
out_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "summary_auc_decay"
out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

fig.savefig(out_dir / "fig_summary_auc_decay.pdf", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
fig.savefig(out_dir / "fig_summary_auc_decay.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

pdf_size = (out_dir / "fig_summary_auc_decay.pdf").stat().st_size
png_size = (out_dir / "fig_summary_auc_decay.png").stat().st_size
print(f"PDF: {pdf_size/1024:.1f} KB | PNG: {png_size/1024:.1f} KB")
assert pdf_size > 10 * 1024, f"PDF too small: {pdf_size}"
assert png_size > 30 * 1024, f"PNG too small: {png_size}"
print("OK")

MVP Pilot Saturation Study — Complete Pipeline (Steps 2-5)

Generates recursive depth chains from C4 seed data using Qwen2.5-1.5B,
extracts statistical features, and runs distinguishability analysis.

Input:  C4 validation split (streamed from HuggingFace)
Output: data/depth_{0..K}.jsonl, data/features.csv, results/*.json + summary.txt

Key deps: torch, transformers, datasets, scipy, lightgbm, sklearn, tqdm
"""

import argparse
import json
import logging
import math
import os
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
from scipy import stats
from tqdm import tqdm

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
    datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
)
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility: simple 4-gram BLEU (no nltk dependency)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ngrams(tokens, n):
    return [tuple(tokens[i : i + n]) for i in range(len(tokens) - n + 1)]


def simple_bleu(candidate_tokens, reference_tokens, max_n=4):
    """Compute sentence-level BLEU up to max_n grams with brevity penalty."""
    if len(candidate_tokens) == 0:
        return 0.0
    precisions = []
    for n in range(1, max_n + 1):
        cand_ngrams = ngrams(candidate_tokens, n)
        ref_ngrams = ngrams(reference_tokens, n)
        if not cand_ngrams:
            precisions.append(0.0)
            continue
        ref_counts = Counter(ref_ngrams)
        clipped = 0
        cand_counts = Counter(cand_ngrams)
        for ng, cnt in cand_counts.items():
            clipped += min(cnt, ref_counts.get(ng, 0))
        precisions.append(clipped / len(cand_ngrams))
    if any(p == 0 for p in precisions):
        return 0.0
    log_avg = sum(math.log(p) for p in precisions) / max_n

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path

# 95% CI lower bounds from exp_007_bootstrap_ci (1000 resamples)
AUC_DATA = {
    "Qwen-rw": [0.9946, 0.6859, 0.5795, 0.5333, 0.5238],
    "Pythia":   [0.9921, 0.6454, 0.5417, 0.5041, 0.5021],
    "OLMo":     [0.9964, 0.6045, 0.5399, 0.4973, 0.4932],
    "Qwen-cont":[0.9963, 0.6015, 0.5511, 0.5308, 0.5035],
}

STYLES = {
    "Qwen-rw":   dict(color="#1f77b4", linestyle="-",  marker="o"),
    "Pythia":     dict(color="#ff7f0e", linestyle="--", marker="s"),
    "OLMo":       dict(color="#2ca02c", linestyle="-.", marker="^"),
    "Qwen-cont":  dict(color="#d62728", linestyle=":",  marker="D"),
}

def compute_kstar(auc_list, theta):
    k = 0
    for auc in auc_list:
        if auc >= theta:
            k += 1
        else:
            break
    return k

thetas = np.arange(0.55, 0.701, 0.01)

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.size": 11,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.8,
    "xtick.direction": "in",
    "ytick.direction": "in",
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

for name, aucs in AUC_DATA.items():
    ks = [compute_kstar(aucs, t) for t in thetas]
    ax.step(thetas, ks, where="post", label=name,
            linewidth=1.8, markersize=4, **STYLES[name])

ax.axvline(x=0.60, color="grey", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.7)
ax.text(0.605, 4.6, r"$\theta=0.60$", color="grey", fontsize=9, va="top")

ax.set_xlabel(r"Threshold $\theta$")
ax.set_ylabel(r"$K^*(\theta)$")
ax.set_xlim(0.545, 0.705)
ax.set_ylim(-0.2, 5.5)
ax.set_yticks(range(6))
ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="none")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e0e0e0", linewidth=0.5)

fig.tight_layout()

out_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "docs" / "paper" / "figures"
out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig(out_dir / "fig_kstar_theta.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
fig.savefig(out_dir / "fig_kstar_theta.png", bbox_inches="tight", dpi=300)
print(f"Saved to {out_dir / 'fig_kstar_theta.pdf'}")
print(f"Saved to {out_dir / 'fig_kstar_theta.png'}")
